seoTitle: Color Palette Generator - Create UI Color Schemes
metaDescription: Free online Color Palette Generator. Instantly generate beautiful, cohesive color schemes (analogous, complementary, monochromatic) for web design and branding.
intro: Starting a new design project but stuck on the colors? Our free Color Palette Generator automatically creates stunning, mathematically balanced color schemes to jumpstart your creativity.
whatIs: The Color Palette Generator is a creative design tool that uses color theory algorithms to generate harmonious sets of colors (palettes). It can generate complementary, analogous, monochromatic, or triadic schemes based on a single starting color.
howToUse: Select a base color using the color picker or by entering a HEX code.
Select the type of harmony rule you want (e.g., Complementary, Analogous).
The tool generates a visual palette of 3 to 5 matching colors.
Click to copy the HEX codes of any color in the generated palette.
howItWorks: The tool converts your base color into the HSL (Hue, Saturation, Lightness) format. It then applies geometric math to the 360-degree color wheel. For a 'complementary' scheme, it adds 180 degrees to the hue. For 'analogous', it adds and subtracts 30 degrees.
workedExample: You input a base color of Blue (Hue 240) and select 'Complementary'. The tool adds 180 to 240, resulting in Hue 60 (which is Yellow). It generates a striking Blue and Yellow palette.
resultInterpretation: The generated palette provides a visually pleasing, cohesive set of colors. You can confidently use these together in a UI design for primary buttons, backgrounds, and accents without them clashing.
useCases: Brand Identity: Creating a logo and marketing materials using a mathematically sound triadic color scheme.
Web Design: Finding a monochromatic scale (light to dark) for button hover states and borders.
Interior Design: Testing color combinations for painting a room and buying matching furniture.
tipsAndLimitations: Don't use every color equally! A good rule in web design is 60-30-10: 60% dominant background color, 30% secondary color, 10% accent (call-to-action) color.
Ensure you test the contrast of your chosen palette to make sure text remains readable.

faq.question: What is an Analogous palette?
faq.answer: Analogous palettes use colors that are right next to each other on the color wheel (like Blue, Blue-Green, and Green). They create a very calm, cohesive, and natural look.

faq.question: What is a Triadic palette?
faq.answer: A triadic palette uses three colors evenly spaced around the wheel (like Red, Yellow, and Blue). It creates a very vibrant and energetic design.

cta: Generate your perfect color palette now!
disclaimer: Palettes are generated based on mathematical color wheel algorithms. Final visual appeal remains subjective to the designer.
